issues.description: The solution repository implements the animal classes with the names SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat, while the problem statement and the template (Main.java) refer to Seal, Pig, and Goat. This class-name/type mismatch is structural: student code and tests will expect classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat, but the solution's concrete types use a different naming convention, which would confuse students and make substitution or referencing by the expected names fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align concrete class names with the problem specification and template by providing Seal, Pig, and Goat classes. Either rename SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat to Seal/Pig/Goat, or add thin wrapper classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat that extend/delegate to the existing Space* implementations so the expected class names exist and behave as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template code refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (the UML and Main.java instantiate Seal, Pig, Goat), but the solution repository implements these concrete animals with different identifiers: SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. This mismatched naming for the same conceptual entities can confuse students who expect to find and implement Seal/Pig/Goat classes as specified in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the concrete class names consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat (and update their internal messages accordingly), or (B) update the problem statement and template to use the SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat names consistently. Prefer renaming solution classes to Seal/Pig/Goat to match the exercise UML and the template Main.java so students can clearly map requirements to implementation.
